svg.title: Rivvon to Android photo frame: the colour and video pipeline
svg.desc: Architecture as of 10 October 2026. Three.js canvas frames branch into the current default FFmpeg WASM export, current optional WebCodecs export, and experimental explicit-YUV WebCodecs path. The diagram separates real sRGB-to-BT.709 limited YCbCr sample conversion from SPS/VUI and MP4 nclx metadata, then follows the unchanged MP4 through Loop, Media3 ExoPlayer, MediaCodec, SurfaceView or TextureView, Android composition and the display panel. It includes measured results, required metadata agreement, environment diagnostics and platform assumptions.
svg.text: Colour conversion, compression, declarations and presentation — architecture as of 10 October 2026
The selected export method determines who converts RGB pixels into video samples.

g.text: Three.js scene → rendered WebGL canvas
Textures + materials + custom ShaderMaterial → LinearSRGBColorSpace / NoToneMapping → legacy numeric-RGB output.
Custom shaders have no explicit final sRGB conversion. Keep this render contract; export interprets displayed canvas bytes as sRGB.
Synthetic frame clock: exact dimensions and frame rate; N = ceil(duration × fps), no duplicate endpoint. Same frames feed the colour chart preview.
sRGB Canvas2D → opaque RGBA8
drawImage onto black matte; optional logo + shadow.
Same compositor with logo enabled or disabled.
getImageData: unpremultiplied sRGB bytes.
Rivvon: RGB → Y′CbCr conversion
Inverse sRGB transfer → linear light → BT.709 OETF.
BT.709 matrix → limited 8-bit I420, Y/Cb/Cr planes.
Y: 16–235; Cb/Cr: 16–240; centred 2×2 chroma.
4:2:0 sampling; sRGB and BT.709 share primaries.
FFmpeg WASM → libx264
Pinned core 0.12.10; software H.264 / AVC.
Encode already-converted yuv420p samples.
Quality presets; bounded batches; no B frames.
AVC → FFmpeg MP4 muxer
SPS/VUI + nclx explicitly 709 / 709 / 709 / limited.
Stream-copy mux; restore exact CFR track clocks.
Mediabunny CanvasSource → VideoFrame
Logo off: WebGL canvas; on: sRGB 2D drawImage.
CanvasSource sets no colour-space override.
Measured canvas input: full-range RGB / sRGB.
WebCodecs VideoEncoder
Browser / OS / GPU / encoder backend converts RGB.
No portable output range / matrix / transfer /
chroma controls. Acceleration preference is a hint.
Canvas output varied: full vs limited, sRGB transfer.
Mediabunny 1.60 MP4 muxer
EncodedVideoChunkMetadata.decoderConfig
.colorSpace → MP4 colr/nclx declarations.
SPS comes from encoder; may omit colour fields.
Conditional missing-SPS repair
FFmpeg h264_metadata + stream copy: fill observed
values only when evidence agrees. Pixels unchanged.

g.aria-label: Same explicit conversion as path A
g.text: Same explicit conversion as path A
sRGB RGBA8 → BT.709 limited 8-bit I420 or NV12.
I420: planar Cb/Cr; NV12: interleaved CbCr.
These are sample layouts, not colour declarations.
Raw VideoFrame → VideoSampleSource
format: I420 / NV12; colorSpace: BT.709,
BT.709 transfer + matrix, fullRange: false.
Mediabunny → WebCodecs native compression.
Avoids canvas RGB conversion; still verify output.
Native AVC → Mediabunny MP4
Inspect actual SPS and nclx; same repair rules.
An input label alone cannot guarantee output.
Reject or convert if samples/declarations differ.
Promising lab result; limited scope
Chrome 155 / Windows / Intel ANGLE: 6 raw-YUV
cases matched target. Android playback pending.
Final inspection + downloadable export report
Check every avcC SPS + MP4 nclx; report range, transfer, matrix, primaries, bit depth and chroma. Path A must match the SDR target.
Capture VideoFrame + encoder colour metadata, browser/OS hints and GL vendor/renderer. Native encoder identity is not exposed.
Preserve dimensions, frame count, clocks and seamless timing; support progress + cancellation. Independent lab checks: ffprobe + trace_headers + decoded chart.

svg.text: Compressed samples and two colour declarations must agree. Declarations do not perform a colour conversion.
MP4 / ISO Base Media File Format — ISO/IEC 14496-12 + AVC carriage ISO/IEC 14496-15

g.text: mdat: compressed AVC video samples
Target: 8-bit Y′CbCr 4:2:0, limited range.
Often called “YUV”; no RGB pixels in the AVC stream.
avcC: SPS/PPS → SPS VUI
SPS: Sequence Parameter Set; optional VUI:
Video Usability Information. H.273/CICP target:
primaries 1 / transfer 1 / matrix 1;
video_full_range_flag = 0.
colr/nclx: MP4 colour declaration
Primaries / transfer / matrix + full-range flag.
Target: 1 / 1 / 1; full_range_flag = 0.
Must agree with SPS and the encoded samples.

svg.text: stts / ctts / edit lists / track timescales preserve presentation timing. WebCodecs exports may declare other values; inspect the actual file.

g.text: Publish / download → Loop local MP4
Gallery transport and local storage carry unchanged bytes; no colour conversion.

svg.text: Loop reports colour metadata; the codec and graphics stack interpret it.

g.aria-label: Loop — Kotlin / Jetpack Compose → Media3 ExoPlayer 1.10.1
g.text: Loop — Kotlin / Jetpack Compose → Media3 ExoPlayer 1.10.1
MediaItem URI → prepare/play; REPEAT_MODE_ONE for looping. The app does no colour correction and passes the MP4 unchanged.
Diagnostics: Format.colorInfo, codec MediaFormat colour keys, decoder name, selected surface, dropped frames and loop timing.
ExoPlayer: MP4 extractor → Format.ColorInfo
Parse avcC/SPS and colr/nclx; construct the input Format.
Media3 1.10.1 prefers bitstream colour over nclx.
nclx fallback when colour space + transfer are absent.
nclx matrix is skipped; colour standard derives from primaries.
MediaCodec → native AVC decoder
Media3 maps Format to MediaFormat; also supplies AVC configuration.
Measured decoder: c2.amlogic.avc.decoder (Amlogic T982).
Decode H.264 into codec output buffers / the selected Surface.
Hardware and driver interpret bitstream + configured colour values.
What the player assumes
Metadata describes the samples correctly; it cannot infer artwork intent.
Missing/conflicting tags can trigger parser or codec defaults.
No universal 601/709 or full/limited fallback across devices.

g.aria-label: Expected Loop diagnostics for the SDR target
g.text: Expected Loop diagnostics for the SDR target
Input: BT709 / Limited / SDR.
Codec: COLOR_STANDARD_BT709 = 1; COLOR_RANGE_LIMITED = 2;
COLOR_TRANSFER_SDR_VIDEO = 3. Android enums differ from CICP codes.
SurfaceView path
Separate Surface / BufferQueue → compositor.
Eligible for a hardware-composer overlay; device-dependent.
MediaCodec renders to the Surface owned by the view.
TextureView path
SurfaceTexture → texture sampled into the app’s GPU composition.
The app’s composed layer then reaches the system compositor.
Additional graphics processing can change presentation.

g.aria-label: Android graphics: SurfaceFlinger → hardware composer / GPU → display engine
g.text: Android graphics: SurfaceFlinger → hardware composer / GPU → display engine
Range expansion, Y′CbCr matrix interpretation and transfer handling occur in the platform presentation path.
Exact conversion stage and metadata priority depend on codec, driver and chosen surface; no single universal RGB boundary.
Output then reaches the panel’s physical transfer response, gamut and calibration. Loop applies no compensating shader.
Photo-frame panel
Visible light → viewer.
Panel calibration / EOTF
has not been measured.

svg.text: Four independent colour properties plus sample layout — and what the comparison has actually established.

g.text: Colour terms / required target
Primaries: RGB chromaticities / white point → BT.709.
Transfer: linear-light ↔ signal curve → BT.709 SDR (not sRGB code 13).
Matrix: R′G′B′ ↔ Y′CbCr coefficients → BT.709 (not 601 / code 6).
Range: numeric scaling → limited / video, rather than full.
Layout: 8-bit 4:2:0; I420 / yuv420p or NV12 are buffer formats.
Measured results / remaining scope
Android: adding SPS alone did not fix the full-range/sRGB colour fault.
FFmpeg conversion restored neutral greys and hues on both surfaces.
Grey 128 displayed as 128 via SurfaceView; 115 via TextureView.
Raw-YUV WebCodecs lab: zero interior chart error, 90 frames / 3 s.
Other native environments + raw-YUV Android tests remain unverified.

Measured device results ≠ calibrated physical-panel measurements
